prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Boundary: receiving to outbound load release. Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk (Cinderbay): checks paperwork/trailer ID/seals, records damage; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note to Yard Gate Controller (Velvetrook: validates arrivals, assigns lane/door, holds risky vehicles; in recovery holds vehicles outside boundary, yard under controlled access until aisle safe); consumes Oversize Load Advisory. Pallet Dimension Scanner (Moonquarry) produces Oversize Load Advisory. Inbound Pallet Buffer: staging only; unavailable to new receipts if access path crosses isolated area. North/South Aisle Stacker Cranes; North (Juniperwake) sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot, uses Slot Reservation Receipt, reports faults. South crane does reduced-speed recovery maneuver, minimal travel. East/West Transfer Conveyors stop if movement compromises boundary. Conveyor Line Controller (Brasshaven) produces Transfer Induction Ticket; holds transfers feeding isolated area. Autonomous Forklift Fleet (Larkspur) produces Forklift Handoff Confirmation; receives hold for routes near recovery area. Outbound Dispatch Sorter receives Dispatch Wave Amendment. Outbound Checkweigh Scale produces Gross Weight Variance Slip. Shipping Documentation Desk. Safety Zone Controller (sets/maintains controlled boundary, blocks entry) and Fire Alarm Panel (Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice) may always stop/restrict movement. Maintenance Release Terminal (Copperfield) produces Crane Service Release Card, records inspection outcome, repairs, authorizer. Warehouse Management System (Morrowglass): authoritative; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment; produces Slot Reservation Receipt; receives occupancy snapshot, reconciles records with sensors, presents recovery plan (travel envelope, stopping point, stop conditions). Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (verifies personnel clear before recovery, reconciles exceptions/holds/access before releasing normal work); spotter (protected location only); drivers, receiving, yard, maintenance staff. Mode: Recovery triggered by position discrepancy, obstruction or safety alarm. Requirements: valid receipt; door only when free; segregate damaged/held pallets; traceable holds; no incompatible allocation under advisory; cranes stop if path invalid; uncertain/duplicate transfers held; stale snapshot holds path; no move without WMS release; faulted crane unavailable; personnel outside envelope during maneuver; unexpected movement/position loss/alarm → immediate stop, reassess, boundary kept until plan rechecked; test confirms stop response and stable position; boundary removed only after pass and aisle clear of personnel/material; failed test keeps inhibited; weight variance needs reweigh/review; forklifts confirm pallet

Document units:
S195: Normal transfers resume in stages, with the first movements observed for unexpected interference or renewed alarms.
S196: Performance is assessed against transfer throughput, task completion time, equipment availability, and the rate of safely resolved exceptions.
S197: The Warehouse Management System records transaction times and reconciles completed movements against the active shift plan.
S198: At shift start, the Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews open alarms, equipment status, and the previous shift's unresolved work.
S199: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor confirms that operators understand current speed limits, exclusion boundaries, and stop-work criteria.
S200: Autonomous Forklift Fleet receives the Transfer Induction Ticket and validates its destination against the assigned route.
S201: Fleet availability is measured as the proportion of scheduled operating time during which vehicles are ready for service.
S202: Route performance is reviewed using completed tasks, travel time, and the number of blocked or delayed movements.
S203: Safety checks verify that personnel detection, audible warnings, and emergency stops respond before production movement begins.
S204: Safety Zone Controller applies the Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice by maintaining the specified exclusion boundary until release criteria are met.
S205: The shift check confirms that the active boundary is visible to operators and enforced by the applicable control logic.
S206: Juniperwake verifies aisle clearance before resuming a stored-pallet movement and stops if an obstruction is detected.
S207: Moonquarry checks each pallet profile against configured dimensional limits and flags measurements outside tolerance.
S208: Dimensional exceptions are held for review rather than passed forward on an assumed measurement.
S209: The Outbound Checkweigh Scale is checked with a known reference load at the start of the shift and after maintenance.
S210: East Transfer Conveyor demonstrates a controlled restart by running empty at reduced speed for one complete cycle before accepting a pallet.
S211: The restart record includes the initiating authorization, observed speed, cycle result, and any alarm response.
S212: The Conveyor Line Controller inhibits feed if the restart cycle is incomplete or a protective device changes state.
S213: Maintenance Release Terminal status is checked before equipment is returned to automatic service.
S214: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor compares reported downtime with control-system event records at each shift review.
S215: Any unexplained difference is investigated before the affected performance measure is accepted.
S216: Near misses, protective stops, and repeated process delays are reviewed for corrective action and accountable ownership.
